_readme.purpose: Scenario scripts for the clearance-state runway monitor (Saturday build). Each scenario is an ordered event list the parser/engine can replay. Times are seconds from the scenario's own t0.

ontology.event: {t, freq, speaker, callsign, kind, runway?, taxiways?, hold_short?, crossing_at?, text_clean, text_raw?, note?}

_readme.claim_discipline: A warning says the engine HAD TWO AUTHORIZATIONS on one runway at time t. It never says the system would have prevented anything.

sources.LGA: Public reporting and the NTSB preliminary for DCA26MA161 (Mar 22, 2026); transmissions re-voiced from the auto-captions of a VASAviation reconstruction (YouTube vxYd_EbKEiw) that Joe Eichelberger pointed to. The captions are a secondary source with speech-recognition errors; text_clean is the standard-phraseology reading, text_raw is the caption as received. Times are mm:ss within that video, not UTC. Do NOT ship the video's audio; re-voice.
sources.BOS: NTSB preliminary report DCA26LA242, Table 1 (primary). Times EDT, June 20, 2026.
sources.TAXI_EXERCISE: United 2384's own taxi clearance from the same LGA night, which is a textbook JO 7110.65 3-7-2 format instruction; used as Joe's node-walk exercise.
sources.CLIPPED: Fictional, written to Schneider's 'the common case is the pilot side clipped' correction.

scenarios.title: LaGuardia, Mar 22, 2026 — crossing clearance issued on runway 4 with a landing clearance active
scenarios.t0_definition: t=0 is the Jazz 646 landing clearance (video 9:50). Negative times are earlier in the same video.
scenarios.frequency_note: The controller was working two frequencies (he says so at video 2:49). The trucks answered 'LaGuardia Tower' when asked whether they were on ground or tower (10:15), so the crossing request and clearance appear to have been on the tower frequency. This is from a secondary source; the NTSB docket will settle it.

expected_flags.b: Truck 1 and company CROSS 04 at D t=40
expected_flags.explain: Runway 4 has an active landing authorization (aircraft number two on final) and a crossing authorization at Delta issued 40 s later. Both require the runway 4 protected area.

NEGATIVE CASE: takeoff clearance on 13 with traffic inside 3 miles for intersecting runway 4 is normal LGA intersecting-runway operation. The compatibility matrix must NOT flag this. Use it as the false-positive test.

scenarios.title: Taxi-route exercise (Joe's node walk): runway 13 via November, Alpha, Echo, hold short runway 4
scenarios.source_note: Real phraseology from UAL2384's second taxi on Mar 22, 2026 (video 4:10). Route segments and hold points come from lga_graph.json.
expected_engine_behaviour: Parse: runway=13, route=[N, A, E], hold_short={runway: 04, at: E}.
Trace N→A→E on the graph; E crosses runway 4/22, so the segment E-west-of-4/22 requires a hold boundary: hold short of 4 at E. Controller DID issue it (no 'missing hold' warning).
Expect a readback that names 'hold short runway 4'. Received at +11 s (no 'readback missing' warning).
Next expected event: 'holding short of runway 4' report (not captured) → then a crossing clearance 'cross runway 4 at Echo' → then crossing complete → then runway 13 line-up/takeoff.
Variant A (missing hold): replay with the controller saying 'Runway 13, November, Alpha, Echo' only → warning: route crosses runway 4 at E, no hold-short issued.
Variant B (discrepant readback): pilot reads back 'hold short runway 13' → warning: readback names a different runway.
Variant C (unclosed crossing): crossing issued, no 'crossing complete' within 90 s → reminder: close out the crossing; runway 4 remains reserved.

scenarios.title: The common case (Schneider): pilot's readback is clipped; the hold-short is in the clipped part
expected_engine_behaviour: Instruction parsed with hold_short={runway: 04, at: D}.
Readback audio is clipped before 'hold short'; parser emits READBACK with confidence 0.41 and hold_short=null.
Engine: acknowledged state for the hold boundary = UNKNOWN (never 'acknowledged'). Warning: 'hold short runway 4 at Delta not heard in readback (clipped)'.
Controller re-issues; full readback heard; acknowledged=true. No runway conflict is ever claimed.
